newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open weak, Tianjin shines.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open weak, Tianjin shines.

text.p: Singapore shares were weaker in mid-morning trade on Friday with focus on debutante Tianjin Zhongxin Pharmaceutical Group Corp, dealers said.
The Chinese drug firm, responsible for the bulk of the market activity, hit a high of US$1.05 against its initial public offer price at US$0.68.
At 0155 GMT, it was trading at US$0.955 and volume was an active 36 million shares.
"There is a lot of retail interest and brokers participating in Tianjin. It is riding on it Chinese-links and price-wise, people like it because it is below US$1," a local dealer said.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index was down 2.01 points at 1,987.79. Tunrover was about 55 million, with 45 gainers to 85 losers.
Shipping firm Osprey Maritime adjusted lower as it went ex-rights. It was down S$0.58 (US$0.41) at S$1.73. Brokers said this was slightly below its theoretical ex-rights price of S$1.88.
Plastics maker Showpla Asia also went ex-rights and adjusted down US$0.12 to US$0.28.
Soft drink firm Yeo Hiap Seng stabilised after its sharp fall on Thursday. It was up 10 cents at S$5.15.
